subject: Follow-up: Harborline pilot TCO sketch and constrained-budget options
messages:
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Ross <ethan.ross@harborline.co>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 18:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Harborline pilot TCO sketch and constrained-budget options

Hi Ethan —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and the pragmatic next steps so we all have the same frame: you mentioned the two primary pressures for Harborline are (1) monthly inference spend runway limited by a fixed budget for Q3, and (2) a strict latency SLO for customer-facing fraud checks (p95 under 200ms).

Key pain points we heard
- Token burn from long contextual prompts across customer sessions (~4–6k tokens per request during peak flows).
- Currently no prefix caching; repeated context (KVs) for returning users is re-sent each request.
- Existing model-hosting has poor throughput at 99th percentile which drives you toward smaller model variants, but you want to avoid meaningful quality regressions.

Goals you shared
- Demonstrate a pilot that reduces per-call token cost by >=40% while keeping p95 latency <200ms for the majority of flows.
- Fit the pilot within an incremental monthly spend of ~$15k–20k (you said procurement gate is in that window).
- Produce a short ROI snapshot for the CFO showing six-month payback under conservative user growth.

Our recommended short pilot (3 weeks, scoped)
- Approach: 2-stage pilot: (A) Lightweight integration + KV/prefix caching + batching for non-real-time paths; (B) Canary serving of a quantized variant for latency-sensitive paths with auto-fallback.
- Expected levers and approximate impact (first-order)
  - Prefix/KV caching: 20–30% token reduction for returning sessions.
  - Micro-batching for async/near-real-time pipelines: 10–25% cost reduction depending on concurrency shape.
  - Quantized model variant for hot path: 15–25% GPU cost reduction at minor quality delta (we’ll run evals).
- Pilot deliverables: integration checklist, cost TCO model (attached), p95 latency runs, and a short quality comparison report.

Next steps (agreed on call)
1) I’ll share a preliminary TCO workbook and pilot scope by end of day (attached).
2) You’ll introduce procurement to the thread so we can line up a short reserved-capacity quote if needed.
3) If procurement bandwidth is limited, we proposed a constrained-budget option where we cap throughput and prioritize caching+baching only — likely fits the $15k–20k window.

Attachments: [Attachment: harborline_tco_model.xlsx (Excel, 240 KB)], [Attachment: pilot-scope-3week.pdf (PDF, 120 KB)]

Open questions for procurement / finance we should pre-answer
- Are you able to sign a short-term reserved capacity (30–60 days) or prefer pay-as-you-go + cap?
- Any legal/compliance docs required for the pilot (SOC-2 snapshot was mentioned on the call)?

I’ll be on PTO Wed–Thu but reachable if something urgent pops up.

Thanks — looking forward to the intro.

Best,
Lukas Meyer
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
[l: +1 415 555 0142]
From: Ethan Ross <ethan.ross@harborline.co>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Harborline pilot TCO sketch and constrained-budget options

Thanks Lukas — solid recap and appreciate the clear levers. A few quick clarifications:

- That conservative $15k–20k is what I can get approved for a pilot without additional CFO sign-off; if we need reserved capacity we’ll need a written price/term for procurement.
- We do need the SOC-2 snapshot, but can accept a short attestation for the pilot.
- Our procurement lead is cc’d here (procurement@harborline.co). Can you send a quote that shows (a) pay-as-you-go with a throttled cap and (b) short reserved capacity 30d cost so they can compare?

Also curious on one technical point: if we enable prefix caching, do we need schema changes in our API or is it handled in the SDK?

Ethan
Head of ML Engineering
Harborline Finance

On Mon, May 25, 2026 at 6:12 PM Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap...
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
To: procurement@harborline.co
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ethan Ross <ethan.ross@harborline.co>
Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Harborline pilot quote options (paygo cap vs 30d reserved)

Hi Harborline procurement team —

Per Ethan’s intro, attaching the quick quote options so you can see the delta between a pay-as-you-go approach with a hard usage cap and a 30-day reserved capacity option. High-level:

- Pay-as-you-go with cap: no term commitment; we configure token/req cap at the account level. Good if you want minimal legal friction. Example estimate: $18k/mo budget cap expected to yield ~40% token savings with caching+batching enabled.
- 30d reserved variant: modestly cheaper unit token cost (~12% lower) but requires a short PO; recommended if you expect consistent daily throughput.

I’ve included the same TCO workbook (attached) with both scenarios and a one-page ROI assuming 6 months of steady-state. Please let us know which format you prefer and any procurement billing constraints.

Attachments: [Attachment: harborline_tco_model.xlsx (Excel, 240 KB)]

If helpful we can schedule a 30-minute procurement walk-through tomorrow to step through the quote.

Best,
Lukas
From: procurement@harborline.co
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Harborline pilot quote options (paygo cap vs 30d reserved)

Thanks — procurement here. Quick notes:
- Please send a formal quote (PDF) for both options with line-item pricing and the PO instructions. We’ll need an SOC-2 snapshot as an appendix.
- For speed, the pay-as-you-go with a cap is preferred (lower legal overhead). If the cost delta is >10% vs reserved we’ll re-evaluate.
- Our billing team requires vendor W-9 (we’ll follow up over separate channel).

Can you send the quote and SOC-2 doc by EOD today? We’re targeting a decision this week.

procurement@harborline.co
